gaps.name: Spouse Health Cover
gaps.whyNow: Marriage means shared healthcare needs. Adding your spouse to a health plan prevents one person's medical emergency from becoming a joint financial crisis.

gaps.name: Term Life Top-up
gaps.whyNow: With a spouse now financially connected to you, your existing life cover may no longer be sufficient to protect both of you.

gaps.name: Joint Savings Plan
gaps.whyNow: Starting a household together brings shared expenses. A joint savings plan helps build a financial buffer for your new life.

gaps.name: Child Health Rider
gaps.whyNow: Newborns and young children need frequent medical attention. A dedicated child health rider covers paediatric care without eating into your main policy.

gaps.name: Education Savings Plan
gaps.whyNow: Education costs rise faster than inflation. Starting early gives compounding time to build a meaningful education fund.

gaps.name: Term Life Increase
gaps.whyNow: A new dependent means your existing life cover needs to stretch further — enough to support your child for 20+ years if needed.

gaps.name: Comprehensive Motor Insurance
gaps.whyNow: Third-party insurance is mandatory but doesn't cover damage to your own vehicle. Comprehensive cover protects against theft, accidents, and natural disasters.

gaps.name: Personal Accident Cover
gaps.whyNow: Road accidents are a leading cause of injury. A personal accident policy covers medical bills and income loss if you're hurt while driving.

gaps.name: Home Insurance
gaps.whyNow: Your home is likely your largest asset. Home insurance protects against fire, floods, theft, and structural damage.

gaps.name: Home Loan Protection Plan
gaps.whyNow: If you have a home loan, this plan ensures your family isn't burdened with EMIs if something happens to you.

gaps.name: Contents Insurance
gaps.whyNow: Furnishing a new home is expensive. Contents insurance covers your appliances, electronics, and valuables against damage or theft.
